- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peaks, especially in early/medium horizon.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates or fails to capture sharp drops; increase early-period lows and adjust downward momentum.
- After a spike in price or sentiment, model frequently overshoots in the next 5–10 days; apply a 10–20% downward correction to forecasted peaks.
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias in medium-term (15–30d) forecasts; if history shows tight clustering, avoid extreme outliers in forecast.
- Sentiment spikes (e.g., 1.00) correlate with model overconfidence; reduce forecast volatility when sentiment is high, especially in short-term (1–7d) horizon.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and price history is stable, model tends to drift upward; apply a downward bias of 5–15% to avoid false momentum.
